study_identification.author_journal_year: Fang et al., Journal of Affective Disorders, 2024
study_identification.title: Individualized gray matter morphological abnormalities uncover two robust transdiagnostic biotypes

study_characteristics.study_objective: This study aimed to identify distinct transdiagnostic subtypes based on individualized gray matter morphological abnormalities compared to normal expectations using normative modeling. The goal was to examine the reproducibility and generalizability of identified subtypes across unseen patients and disorders, and investigate their disease epicenters and molecular/genetic underpinnings.

dataset_name.answer: UCLA Consortium for Neuropsychiatric Phenomics (CNP); COBRE; DIRECT (site 20); SALD

hc_n.answer: Discovery: 110; Validation 1: 73; Validation 2: 251; SALD (for structural covariance network): 492

hc_age.answer: Discovery: mean 31.26 (sd 8.66); Validation 1: mean 36.07 (sd 13.08); Validation 2: mean 39.64 (sd 15.87); SALD: 19-80 years

preprocessing_pipeline.answer: CAT12 toolbox; voxel-based morphometry; 6-mm FWHM Gaussian smoothing; TIV recorded

quality_checking_detail.answer: Participants with missing behavioral scores/images or signal dropouts in the cerebellum were excluded. Discovery dataset: excluded participants to achieve final cohort of 224 participants from initial 272. Validation 1: excluded participants with poor image quality or missing data. Validation 2: exclusion criteria applied for serious encephalopathy.

site_effect_handling_detail.answer: Single-site datasets were used for each validation dataset to prevent multi-site effects. Discovery dataset (CNP) is from UCLA single site. Validation dataset 1 (COBRE) is single-site. Validation dataset 2 used site 20 of DIRECT (single-site dataset with the largest sample size) to prevent multi-site effects on the results.

software_tool.answer: Not explicitly stated (methods follow Marquand et al., 2016; Wolfers et al., 2018; Han et al., 2023a)

response_variable.answer: Regional gray matter volumes (GMVs) from 246 brain regions

predictor_effects.answer: Age and sex were used as predictors in the Gaussian process regression model. The specific fixed/random effects specification is not explicitly stated in the methods.

nm_vldtn_handle_ns.reason: The study addresses some nuisance structure by including age, sex, and total intracranial volume (TIV) as covariates in statistical analyses. However, the normative model itself only uses age and sex as predictors. Site effects are handled by design (using single-site datasets) rather than statistical modeling. Other potential nuisance factors such as motion, scanner quality metrics, or heteroscedasticity are not explicitly addressed in the normative modeling framework.
nm_vldtn_handle_ns.supporting_text: We trained a Gaussian process regression model to estimate the normative range of regional gray matter volumes (GMVs) based on age and sex in HCs. ... we examined the gray matter morphological abnormalities relative to HCs using a two-sample t-test, with sex, age, and total intracranial volume (TIV) as covariates.

nm_vldtn_same_domain_nonindep.reason: The paper does not report validation metrics using non-independent data from the same domain (e.g., cross-validation, train-test split within the same dataset). The normative model was trained on healthy controls from the discovery dataset and directly applied to patients without reporting within-domain validation metrics such as explained variance, MSLL, or similar performance measures on held-out healthy controls.
nm_vldtn_same_domain_nonindep.supporting_text: No specific text describes within-domain validation using cross-validation or similar approaches.

nm_vldtn_same_domain_indep.reason: The study does not report validation of the normative model using independent healthy control data from the same domain. While the study uses validation datasets 1 and 2, these are described as validating the 'subtyping results' rather than validating the normative model performance itself. No metrics such as explained variance, MSLL, correlation, or prediction accuracy are reported for the normative model on independent healthy control samples.
nm_vldtn_same_domain_indep.supporting_text: The reproducibility and generalizability analyses focus on subtyping results (ARI values, clustering consistency) rather than normative model performance.

nm_vldtn_diff_domain.reason: The study demonstrates that subtypes identified using the normative model in the discovery dataset can generalize to different datasets (COBRE for schizophrenia, DIRECT for depression), which constitutes a form of cross-domain validation. The cluster centroids from the discovery dataset successfully predicted subtypes in validation datasets (ARI=0.64 for schizophrenia, ARI=0.30 for depression). However, this validates the subtyping framework rather than the normative model's predictive performance itself. The normative model appears to be re-trained separately for each dataset rather than applied across domains, though this is not entirely clear from the methods description.
nm_vldtn_diff_domain.supporting_text: We used the cluster centroids of the two subtypes to infer subtype labels for patients with schizophrenia from another independent dataset... the ARI between the predicted subtype labels and the true labels obtained using the aforementioned procedures [was 0.64]... we investigated whether these identified subtypes could extend to other psychiatric disorders such as depression... The ARI between true subtyping results and those inferred by the cluster centroids of the identified transdiagnostic subtypes obtained using the discovery dataset was 0.30.
nm_vldtn_diff_domain.location: Section 2.3 Reproducibility and generalizability analysis; Results section 3.3

clinical_dataset.answer: Discovery: UCLA Consortium for Neuropsychiatric Phenomics (CNP); Validation 1: COBRE; Validation 2: DIRECT (site 20)

diseases_studied.answer: Schizophrenia (SCZ); Bipolar Disorder (BD); Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD); Depression

clinical_groups_n.answer: Discovery: Sch:37; BD:40; ADHD:37; Validation 1: Sch:61; Validation 2: Depression:282

clinical_groups_age.answer: Discovery: Sch mean 35.54 (sd 9.08); BD mean 34.78 (sd 9.24); ADHD mean 31.22 (sd 10.11); Validation 1: Sch mean 36.57 (sd 12.97); Validation 2: Depression mean 38.74 (sd 13.65)

clinical_groups_sex.answer: Discovery: Sch F 42.50% M 57.50%; BD F 45.95% M 54.05%; ADHD F 48.18% M 51.82%; Validation 1: Sch F 21.31% M 78.69%; Validation 2: Depression F 64.89% M 35.11%

deviation_metric.answer: Z-scores representing individualized gray matter morphological abnormalities. Z-scores were calculated to quantify deviations of predicted GMVs from normal distributions. Positive Z scores indicated higher GMVs in patients compared to HCs, and vice versa.

clinical_application_and_analysis.association_analysis: K-means clustering algorithm was used to identify transdiagnostic subtypes using Z-scores as features and squared Euclidean distance as the distance metric. Silhouette values were used to determine optimal number of subtypes (2-10 range tested). Two-sample t-tests were performed to examine gray matter morphological abnormalities relative to HCs (with sex, age, and TIV as covariates). Reproducibility: Adjusted Rand Index (ARI) was calculated between subtyping results from random subsamples (90%) and full dataset (repeated 1000 times). Validation with HYDRA algorithm. Generalizability: Cluster centroids were used to infer subtype labels in independent datasets; ARI calculated between predicted and true labels. Disease epicenter mapping: Pearson correlation between regional abnormalities and structural covariance network-informed abnormalities. Permutation testing (10,000 times) for significance. Multilinear models constructed between neurotransmitter receptor/transporter profiles and gray matter differential patterns (permutation testing with FDR correction). Dominance analysis performed to assess relative importance of predictors. Pearson correlation coefficients calculated between gray matter morphological abnormalities and transcriptional profiles of inflammation-related genes (p<0.05 after FDR correction).
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_brief: Two robust transdiagnostic subtypes with opposite gray matter morphological abnormality patterns were identified, showing distinct disease epicenters and differential associations with excitatory versus inhibitory neurotransmitter receptors, with subtype 2 showing correlation with inflammation-related gene expression.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_detailed: The study identified two transdiagnostic subtypes across psychiatric disorders (schizophrenia, bipolar disorder, ADHD) with contrasting gray matter morphological abnormality patterns. Subtype 1 (n=70: SCZ=14, BD=35, ADHD=31) showed predominantly increased GMV, while subtype 2 (n=44: SCZ=23, BD=15, ADHD=6) demonstrated widespread GMV reductions. Reproducibility analysis showed high stability (average ARI=0.96±0.25e-2 between full sample and random 90% subsamples over 1000 iterations). The subtypes were replicated using HYDRA algorithm (ARI=0.42 between methods). Generalizability to independent datasets showed ARI=0.64 for schizophrenia (validation dataset 1) and ARI=0.30 for depression (validation dataset 2). Both subtypes showed significant correlations between regional abnormalities and structural covariance network-informed differences (subtype 1: r=0.31, p_FDR<0.001; subtype 2: r=0.59, p_FDR<0.001). Distinct disease epicenters were identified: subtype 1 showed epicenters in hippocampus, parahippocampal gyrus, inferior occipital gyrus, thalamus, striatum, precuneus, and insula; subtype 2 in anterior cingulate cortex, precentral gyrus, middle occipital gyrus, striatum, insula, and parahippocampal gyrus. Multilinear models linking neurotransmitter receptors/transporters to gray matter abnormalities showed adjusted R²=0.16 (F-statistic(246,226)=3.41) for subtype 1 and adjusted R²=0.59 (F-statistic(246,226)=19.70) for subtype 2 (all FDR-corrected p<0.001). Dominance analysis revealed 5HT1A as key for subtype 1 and mGluR5 for subtype 2. Excitatory receptors predominantly influenced subtype 1 abnormalities while inhibitory receptors dominated in subtype 2. Gray matter abnormalities in subtype 2 correlated significantly with transcriptional profiles of inflammation-related genes (r=-0.15, p_FDR=0.035), while subtype 1 did not show this correlation (r=-0.11, p_FDR=0.092).
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_limitations: Limited number of psychiatric disorders included in the analysis, though generalizability to unseen disorders was demonstrated. Lack of sufficient clinical information (education level, alcohol use, medication dosage) prevented examination of their effects on clustering outcomes. Comorbidities were not accounted for in the analysis. Small sample size in discovery dataset may have limited detection of structural abnormalities in subtype 1 (though validation datasets replicated the opposite differential patterns). Cross-sectional design limits understanding of temporal trajectories and causal relationships.
clinical_application_and_analysis.application_notes: The study demonstrates that individualized deviation maps from normative modeling can identify clinically meaningful transdiagnostic subtypes. The identified subtypes show distinct molecular and genetic underpinnings (differential associations with excitatory vs inhibitory receptors, inflammation-related genes), suggesting different biological mechanisms. The framework successfully generalized from three primary disorders (schizophrenia, bipolar disorder, ADHD) to predict subtypes in depression, supporting transdiagnostic utility. The use of structural covariance networks to identify disease epicenters provides insights into pathological progression trajectories. Future applications could explore whether these subtypes have implications for treatment selection and whether they hold validity across a broader spectrum of psychiatric conditions. The inflammation association with subtype 2 may inform targeted treatment approaches.
